verdicts.reasons: Both answers say clearly that the model swap is not enough. Both also give per-test attempt limits, repeat detection, git commit and rollback against regressions, protection of the test files, and the idea of escalating to Opus, all in Russian with Python code. B's skeleton puts every stopping condition the rubric asks for into one runnable loop: a global MAX_ITERS, a dollar budget, a NO_PROGRESS_LIMIT counter, a pytest timeout and a final report. A has no global iteration cap and no failing-count progress check, and its wall-clock limit is declared but never enforced in the loop. A's diagnosis of the rounding problem and its NEEDS_HUMAN prompt exit are a bit richer, but that does not quite make up for the gaps in its stopping conditions.

Both answers meet every rubric item in Russian, with bounded loops, repeat detection, per-test give-up and git checkpoint/rollback; A's single loop is slightly more coherent (explicit max iterations and a global no-progress counter). B edges ahead on practical value: a wall-clock limit, an explicit NEEDS_HUMAN exit in the prompt for the ambiguous rounding case, anti-cheating checks for skip/xfail, and concrete diagnostic commands to verify flakiness and test tampering before the rewrite. B has a slightly more concrete OOM check and log excerpt, but that does not quite make up the gap.

B also adds a direct curl reproduction, profiling and caching of the export, and post-change verification steps, which makes it somewhat more actionable.

Both answers meet every rubric item in nearly the same way: a hedged range plus a padded window, a timed rehearsal on a restored copy multiplied by 1.5, a correct description of the full rewrite and index rebuild under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, and an online migration built on a new column, a sync trigger and a batched backfill. errors_with: Switchover drops the default on id_old, but id_old keeps NOT NULL after the PK is dropped in PG16, so inserts would fail with a not-null violation

verdicts.reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item with nearly identical structure: an explicit estimate framed as non-binding, a rehearsal on a restored copy, a correct explanation of the rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, and an online migration template. A's switchover script is more correct: it drops the default on the old id column, while B leaves id_old integer with DEFAULT nextval, so every insert consumes two sequence values and inserts would fail once the sequence passes 2^31. B's 1.5-4h estimate with a 6h window is somewhat optimistic for 245 GB plus WAL and index rebuilds, although it is hedged; its planning-meeting script is a nice touch but does not outweigh the migration bug.
errors_without: Switchover leaves DEFAULT nextval on the renamed integer id_old column, which causes double sequence consumption and eventual integer overflow errors on insert
